https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cddv.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Police used a robot to defuse an explosive device found on a drone at Leipzig Airport earlier this month By Bethany Bell Reporting from Leipzig Published 25 August 2026 German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has warned that those responsible for drone attacks and other hostile acts against Germany, including a recent case at Leipzig Airport, would "pay a price". Merz said the incident showed Germany was "facing a very real threat" and was increasingly becoming a target. On 4 August, a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes. However, it failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty. Police defused the explosives and believe a second drone may have collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. Security experts have speculated that Russia may have been responsible. The German government has made no direct accusations. Moscow has denied involvement. Leipzig/Halle Airport is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carry most of the country's aerial cargo. It is also a major hub for logistics group DHL. "We have problems, some of which stem from outside the country, and which we must not ignore," Merz said. "Attackers are increasingly ruthless, accepting even severe property damage, and even injuries and fatalities." According to German reports, investigators have since found a third drone near Leipzig airport. Public broadcasters NDR, WDR and the SÃ¼ddeutsche Zeitung newspaper also reported that traces of the military explosive hexogen were found nearby. Speaking on the margins of a government coalition retreat at Neuhardenberg, Merz said the government was working closely with the security authorities on the case and would release more details soon. Image source, EPA Image caption, Merz reaffirmed German backing for Ukraine in its conflict with Russia Merz also vowed to "stay the course" supporting Ukraine in its fight against Russia's invasion. "The government is continuing its support for Ukraine with steadfast resolve," he said. "Today, we are its strongest supporter - not to prolong the war, but to force peace talks." Germany, he said, was initiating a range of measures to better protect itself against such attacks. These include stronger drone defences and plans to empower security services to strike back against attackers at home and abroad, for example by hacking their computer servers. There has been a series of unauthorised drone flights in recent months over sensitive sites in Germany including military bases, airports, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies. Police have warned that the overflights could have been organised by Russian agents. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/13/one-.text: One person has died and 102 were rescued on Sunday from a ferry that went missing off of the Indonesian island of Java, rescue officials said.The vessel, which was carrying 243 people, had been sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo when it encountered bad weather."We have carried out efforts to search for victims to the fullest extent. There were passengers who...had already been successfully evacuated by the units at the scene. We can inform you that the total number of evacuated passengers is 103 people," local search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana told reporters, adding that one of the passengers had died.Sudayana said rescuers faced waves of up to 2.5 metres as they fought to reach the ferry amid "extremely risky" conditions for vessels."Even our Basarnas vessel, which is 40 meters long, is at great risk," he said, referring to Indonesia's Search and Rescue Agency.It comes after a speedboat carrying eight people, including five journalists covering the recent eruption of Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatoa, went missing earlier this week. The search for the vessel remains ongoing.The Southeast Asian nation is made up of more than 17,000 islands, with boats providing a common and important form of transport.This is a developing story. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: SpaceX rocket launch creates glowing 'space jellyfish' cloud – video Florida SpaceX rocket launch causes stunning ‘jellyfish cloud’ visible off US east coast Expanding plume of fuel exhaust crystalized in the sky and reflected sunlight off frozen particles after Florida launch Richard Luscombe in Miami Wed 14 Oct 2026 14.15 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 16.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A SpaceX rocket provided a stunning pre-dawn display over Florida as a egiant, luminescent “jellyfish cloud” spread for miles, caused by an expanding plume of fuel exhaust crystalizing in the sky and reflecting sunlight off the frozen particles. The phenomenon occurred shortly after Tuesday’s 6.33am ET launch of the Falcon 9 rocket carrying cargo to the International Space Station. The timing of the blastoff, 48 minutes before sunrise at Florida’s Cape Canaveral space force station, provided a perfect example of the colorful effect only fully visible from Earth during dusk and dawn launches. The rocket’s north-eastern trajectory over the Atlantic also allowed residents of eastern states from Georgia to New York to enjoy the spectacle. Nasa posted photographs of the jellyfish cloud on X , the social media platform owned by the SpaceX chief executive, Elon Musk. Among the hundreds of replies were images taken by sky watchers across multiple states. Those who missed Tuesday’s dazzling celestial show have another opportunity to view one next Monday, 19 October, when another SpaceX Falcon 9 is scheduled to lift off from the same space force station pad. An hour-long launch window for the satellite-deployment mission opens at 6.30am ET, little more than a half-hour before the 7.01am sunrise.
